question.en: Discuss the role of the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) in promoting sustainable rural development in developing nations like India.

introduction.en: The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) is a specialized UN agency and international financial institution established in 1977 to eradicate poverty and hunger in rural areas of developing countries.
introduction.hi: The International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) is a specialized UN agency and international financial institution established in 1977 to eradicate poverty and hunger in rural areas of developing countries.

body.en: In India, IFAD focuses on empowering smallholder farmers through climate-resilient agricultural practices, improving market access, and supporting tribal communities. By providing low-interest loans and grants, IFAD helps bridge the gap in rural infrastructure and financial inclusion, ensuring that marginalized populations can participate in the agricultural value chain.
body.hi: In India, IFAD focuses on empowering smallholder farmers through climate-resilient agricultural practices, improving market access, and supporting tribal communities. conclusion.en: IFAD's targeted interventions are crucial for India's rural transformation, directly contributing to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals 1 (No Poverty) and 2 (Zero Hunger).
